Specific Objective
  • Upon completion of this worksheet, the student will have demonstrated a sound fundamental knowledge of internal combustion engine operation, proper assembly and disassembly of the engine, proper measuring and machining practices, and how to set up an engine to factory specifications.
  • The student must be able to demonstrate these skills upon instructor request.

PART B  —  CLICK TO EXPAND / COLLAPSE
Disassembly & Assembly Rules to Live — or Die — By
Remember To:
  • Keep all bolts separated
  • Mark all wires and hoses
  • Keep components in correct order (mark heads, right and left, pushrods in order, etc.) and store in trunk of car if possible
  • Make all checks listed in this worksheet
  • Mark connecting rods and caps — don’t mix up caps!
  • Mark all main caps
  • Clean all parts thoroughly
  • Assemble engine using lubricant No. 105 lube
  • Make sure all parts have been torqued to specifications
  • Pre-lube engine before starting
  • Static time the motor
  • Start motor and dynamic-time the engine as soon as possible; do NOT crank the engine excessively on first start-up
  • Shut off motor and let engine cool; pressure check the cooling system and recheck oil/coolant levels before the first road test
